title: UAS-11: Uncommanded Position Jump — Lakeshore Flight Area

fields.organization: Harwick UAS Operations Group — Flight Operations
fields.location: Lakeshore Flight Area, meadow west end, near lodge patio
fields.weather: Clear, 72°F, wind 6 mph from the west
fields.summary: This is the Payload Operator on UAS-11. PANEL CLEAR confirmed. The aircraft is now 120 meters east of the meadow, over the lodge patio. DAA-1 shows position as 43.1724°N, 77.5631°W. RTK-1 has a full fix. The aircraft telemetry shows a 150-meter jump in latitude under clear sky. The flight line is east–west over the meadow. This does not match the field. The aircraft is not on the flight line.

findings.notes: 150m east jump in latitude under clear sky; not on assigned east–west line
Full RTK correction received at launch point and during flight
Disagrees with known aircraft telemetry and field coordinates
PAY-01 receiving, calibration file date matches FOM-2
VO on site, notifying of anomaly
No one within 100m of launch zone
CT-1 to CT-4 and RP-1 deployed, no obstruction
120m (394 ft) AGL; exceeds standard multispectral line altitude of 120m and exceeds 400 ft AGL limit in Class G airspace

actionsTaken: Declared 'ABORT' to RPIC and VO via intercom
Switched to attitude mode on GCS-04
Notified Incident Commander (IC), Technical Lead (TL), and Safety Officer (ASO) via secure channel
recommendations: Immediately land UAS-11 in manual mode
Preserve GCS-04 and RTK-1 telemetry logs for forensic analysis
Secure launch area and monitor for unauthorized RF emitters
Initiate Section 9.1 incident protocol per ISP C2

title: GCS-02: Unauthorized GCS Detected in Device List

lines.msg: New device entry: GCS-04 (MAC: 915-0A-1F-3C-7D-4E). No record of GCS-04 in fleet register. MAC not in inventory.
RTK-1: GNSS fix lost. Satellite count: 12 → 0. Sky clear. No weather event.
UAS-11: Aircraft GNSS fix lost. Position jumped 150m north. No known motion or wind event.
915 MHz link quality: 94% → 12% in 0.4 seconds. No known interference source.
UAS-11: RTK-1 and aircraft GNSS both lost fix simultaneously under clear sky.
UAS-11: DAA-1 telemetry shows position as 43.1724°N, 77.5631°W. GCS-02 shows 43.1719°N, 77.5635°W.
UAS-11: Home point updated to 43.1721°N, 77.5633°W. No command received from RPIC.
UAS-11: Flight controller received command to set home point. No RPIC input logged.
UAS-11: Command injection detected. Firmware hash matches baseline.
UAS-11: DAA-1 and GCS-02 disagree on aircraft position. Discrepancy: 0.0005° (approx. 55m).
UAS-11: No user input received from RPIC at 09:15:30.
Log export initiated by HUOG-OPS-03. All logs preserved to HUOG-NAS01: /incidents/20261022/GCS-02-091802

title: Radio: Unauthorized GCS Device Detected — UAS-11

lines.text: Ops, I'm trying to re-pair via the OEM app on GCS-02. It says: 'Device ID mismatch. Re-pair required. New device ID: GCS-04. Accept?' I did not send that command. No GCS-04 exists as a separate GCS in the fleet. Is this a spoof?

The system is still showing GCS-04 in the device list. I've checked the fleet roster and baseline. There is no GCS-04 as a standalone ground station. GCS-04 runs the Linux baseline L-2026.2 and is not a command node. This is not a known configuration. I'm not initiating any re-pair. I'm holding the link and waiting for your direction.

title: Radio: White Van at Lodge Parking Pad — Birch Hollow Range

lines.text: Ops, this is Site Manager at Birch Hollow Range. A white van with a rooftop antenna and a 915 MHz transceiver left the lodge parking pad (TP-LFA-LP1) at 09:10. No ID on the vehicle. It was not on the site survey form. The lodge Wi-Fi is on 10.17.40.11.

fields.voiceStyle: Middle-aged male, calm but urgent, slight background wind and distant engine hum

fields.cc: General Manager, Aviation Safety Officer, Client Liaison, Security / CCSO Liaison
fields.subject: INCIDENT DECLARED: UAS-11 915 MHz Link Compromise and GNSS Spoofing
fields.body:
This is an official declaration of a Level 3 incident under HUOG-ISP Section 9.1 (C2 link compromise, interference, or GNSS spoofing).

The HUOG-ERP has been activated. Incident Commander (Ops) is assigned. All roles must now proceed under the HUOG-ERP incident command structure.

The scribe is to begin the incident log immediately at \HUOG-NAS01\ops\incident-log\2026-10-22\UAS-11\ per HUOG-ERP Section 11.3. The digital log and paper copy must be maintained in real time.

All communications, actions, and decisions must be documented. Do not initiate any system resets, reboots, or network disconnections without explicit direction from the Incident Commander or the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead.

This incident is now under full operational control. All roles are to report status updates via the primary command channel and ensure all team members are accounted for in the incident chain.
